description:
Which AI crawlers and assistants (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended…) may crawl a site, each with the deciding robots.txt rule; a homepage probe as AI bots for firewall/CDN blocks; paste-ready robots.txt fixes.

Billing: free.

When to call: 'can ChatGPT / AI bots reach my site', or before blaming content for lost citations. One page's full check: run_technical_audit; agents buying: check_agent_readiness.

Returns { domain, robots_txt, summary: { blocked, limited, training_blocked, unclear, likely_blocked_by_firewall, firewall_unconfirmed, robots_unknown }, bots: [{ bot, owner, purpose, verdict, robots_verdict?, firewall_note?, rule }], firewall_probe, llms_txt_blocked_for, fixes: [{ title, how: append, robots_txt, bots }], cached_at, since_last_check?, suggested_next?, next_step }. limited: a rule keeps the bot off a public page. fixes are lines to append, never a replacement; with a free fix there's no suggested_next. The probe fakes user-agents, with a faked Googlebot as control: refused too means the site likely verifies crawler IPs (firewall_unconfirmed, not blocked; confirm in server logs). suggested_next: one priced step; relay once, run only if the user agrees.

domain.description: Hostname or URL of the site to check, e.g. "acme.com".

name: check_ai_crawlers
title: Check which AI crawlers can reach a site
